replies.text:
Check of commonly-missed items:

- Automated abuse / scraping: design has "The map endpoint takes a delivery id and returns the driver location and phone number" — reachable scraping is already covered by listed threat 1 (harvesting every driver by guessing ids) and threat 3 (load).
- Staff/admin screens showing user-supplied content: design mentions no admin, moderation or support screen, and no file upload — not applicable.
- Privileged actions with no record (delete/refund/role change/money): design describes only GPS sending and a map read; no such action stated — not applicable. A pure "no access log for location lookups" claim would rest on build detail, not design text.
- Personal pages cacheable by browsers, shared proxies or CDNs: design states the endpoint "returns the driver location and phone number" to customers on a live, continuously refreshed map — personal data in a GET response keyed on a guessable id; **not covered** by any listed threat.
- Attacker text flowing into logs, CSV/exports, emails or headers: design names no export, email, SMS or log sink — not applicable.
- Unconfirmed single-reviewer threats: #1 duplicates listed threat 4; #2 duplicates listed threat 1; #4 duplicates listed threat 2; #3 (driver mock-location to claim progress) relies on delivery decisions the design never states ("Customers see the driver on a live map" only) — excluded.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-05",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["driver mobile app", "location ingest", "map endpoint", "customer delivery page"],
    "dataStores": ["driver location store"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["driver phone to backend", "customer browser to map endpoint"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Driver location and phone number cached by browsers, shared proxies or CDNs",
      "scenario": "The map response carries a driver's live coordinates and personal phone number and is fetched repeatedly by the customer's browser for a live map. With no stated no-store/private caching rules, these responses sit in the browser cache on shared or family devices, in corporate proxy caches and in any CDN in front of the endpoint. A later user of the same device or anyone able to read the shared cache retrieves a driver's position history and phone number without ever calling the endpoint or knowing a delivery id.",
      "component": "map endpoint response (delivery id -> driver location + phone)",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "medium", "reach": "many", "harm": "personal_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The map endpoint takes a delivery id and returns the driver location and phone number." },
        { "quote": "Delivery drivers’ phones send GPS location every 10 seconds. Customers see the driver on a live map." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-525"],
      "plainLanguage": "The page showing a driver's location and phone number can be saved in browser or network caches, so someone else using that device or network can read it later.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Mark driver location responses as non-cacheable",
        "given": "a response from the map endpoint containing driver location and phone number",
        "when": "it is returned to a customer's browser through any proxy or CDN",
        "then": "it is sent with Cache-Control: no-store (and private, no caching at shared or CDN layers), so no copy of the driver's location or phone number is retained outside the live request"
      }
    }
  ]
}
